items.prompt: I want to understand the gene regulation in my endometrial cancer samples better.
Run LIONESS co-expression on expr_twins.tsv (it has just two sample columns, one per twin) so that each twin gets their own gene co-expression network.
Can DRAGON fit one partial-correlation network across three omics layers at once (RNA-seq, DNA methylation M-values and RPPA proteomics) for the same 90 ovarian tumours?

For each of our 25 diffuse large B-cell lymphoma patients I need that patient's own TF-to-gene regulatory network, built from the cohort's expression matrix together with a human motif prior and a TF PPI, so I can later compare each TF's targeting between responders and non-responders.

Run LIONESS co-expression on expr_pbmc_vaccine.tsv (genes in rows, 40 donors in columns, header with donor IDs) and give me the aggregate network plus one co-expression network per donor. I only have the expression, no motif or PPI files.

I'd like a network of how about 150 regulators control their target genes across 60 hepatocellular carcinoma samples. I have the expression matrix, a PPI among those regulators, and a regulator-to-target prior from a collaborator's project, but that project studied both RNA-binding proteins and transcription factors, and I'm not sure which of the two lists I was given.

We measured 180 circulating miRNAs (normalized, continuous qPCR values) and 45 plasma cytokines in the same 64 sepsis patients; both tables have samples in rows, identical patient IDs and no missing values. What I want is a separate network for every patient that links miRNAs and cytokines through partial correlations, within and across the two layers, so I can compare survivors with non-survivors patient by patient afterwards.

Can GIRAFFE be run with my own optimizer settings? For our 52 rice leaf samples from the drought trial I want a learning rate of 1e-4, 2,000 iterations and a heavier weight on the PPI term in the loss, because in a pilot the package defaults gave a TF activity matrix that looked over-smoothed and I'd like to see whether these settings change that.
Should I go with BONOBO or LIONESS for my 20 Shank3 knockout and wild-type mouse cortex samples? I'm hoping to learn something about the knockout, but I haven't pinned down what yet.
Should I be using COBRA or CONDOR on our lupus nephritis cohort? I keep seeing both names in NetZoo papers and I'm not sure what either would give me.

Run the TF network inference on expr_alzheimer.tsv (88 donors: 44 AD, 44 controls), motifs_hg38.txt and ppi_tf.txt. The analysis plan just says 'a network for each AD and control', and I can't tell if that means one network per diagnostic group or one network per donor; the person who wrote it is on leave until next month.
Please run the network analysis on expr_sle_monocytes.tsv and send me the results.
Run OTTER on expr_t2d_islets.tsv, seed_W.tsv and ppi_tf.tsv with lam set to 1.5, so co-expression gets even more weight than PPI.
Can I add an L1 (lasso) sparsity penalty to OTTER's objective so that the TF-gene network it returns for my 45 bovine mammary gland samples is sparse, with most edges exactly zero?
Analyze everything in glioma_bundle/ (expression.tsv, methylation.tsv and mutations.csv for 80 gliomas) and tell me what you find.

From our 10x single-cell RNA-seq of differentiating iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, I'd like to order the cells along a pseudotime trajectory and find the branch point where atrial and ventricular fates split.

I want a transcript-metabolite partial-correlation network for 75 NAFLD liver biopsies in which the transcript layer's shrinkage is fixed at 0.3, as in our previous paper, while the metabolite layer's shrinkage is estimated from the data.
Run CONDOR directly on expr_kidney_fibrosis.tsv (gene-by-sample RNA-seq for 64 biopsies) to get gene communities. I don't have any motif or PPI files, just this expression table.
Use the files in shared/hcc_project/ (expr_mrna.tsv, expr_mirna.tsv, motif_hs.txt and targetscan_pairs.txt) and run whichever NetZoo analysis is appropriate.

Run PANDA on tumour_profiles_v2.tsv with motif_hs.txt and ppi_hs.txt. Heads up: our lab saved two genes-by-tumours matrices under similar names, one with log2 expression and one with binary somatic-mutation calls, and I'm not sure which one this is.

Can CONDOR find communities in network_final.tsv, which a postdoc left behind when he moved on? It's a three-column source/target/weight table, but I don't know whether it's the TF-to-gene regulatory network from his PANDA runs or the gene-gene co-expression network he also built.
Call somatic SNVs and indels from tumour_07.bam against its matched normal_07.bam and give me a filtered VCF.

We generated quite a lot of omics on a pig model of septic shock: whole-blood transcriptome, plasma proteome and a few hundred metabolites, sampled at baseline and at 24 hours. I'd like a systems-level view of what is going on in these animals. Where should we start?

Reviewers asked for 'a network analysis' of our placenta study. We have mRNA-seq and small-RNA-seq from 45 preeclampsia and control placentas. Honestly I don't know what kind of network they expect or what it's supposed to show. The two groups are roughly balanced and both libraries come from the same placentas; can you set something up that would satisfy them?

I'd like one regulatory network for my 70 colorectal tumours in which both transcription factors and microRNAs act as regulators of their target genes. I have the gene-by-sample expression matrix, a TF motif prior, a TF-TF PPI, a miRNA-target prior and a file listing the miRNAs, one ID per line, all of which appear in the prior. Nothing per-patient is needed; a single cohort-level network is what goes into the paper.

We have somatic mutation calls and RNA-seq for the same 90 bladder tumours. Is SAMBAR the right thing to run, or one of the network methods like PANDA? I'm open to whatever gives the most interesting result.
Can SAMBAR subtype our 210 hepatocellular carcinomas from the RNA-seq expression matrix? We don't have mutation calls for this cohort, only expression.

Our 140 skeletal-muscle RNA-seq samples (about 18,000 genes after filtering) were sequenced in three runs and come from donors of both sexes. I'd like to see how much of each gene pair's co-expression is associated with sequencing run versus sex, and get an adjusted gene-by-gene co-expression matrix out of it for later network work. Both covariates are already coded as numeric indicator columns in a design table whose rows are exactly the expression sample IDs.

I already have an aggregate TF-to-gene regulatory network for glioblastoma, exported as an edge list with source, target and weight columns; TF and gene IDs don't overlap and the weights were thresholded to be non-negative. Now I want to split it into communities of TFs and their target genes, with the TF-side and gene-side memberships reported separately.
Run SAMBAR on mut_pilot.csv (mutation counts for 5 cholangiocarcinomas) with exon_len.csv, cancer_genes.txt and hallmark.gmt, testing every subtype number from 2 through 8.

Can GIRAFFE give us signed TF-to-gene effects, activation versus repression, for our 40 atopic dermatitis skin biopsies? We have expression, a motif prior and a TF PPI. My supervisor's notes say we need those signed effects for each biopsy separately, but the grant text says one set of signed effects for the whole cohort, and I'm not sure which she actually wants.

Will DRAGON take my paired plasma proteomics and metabolomics tables (both with a header, the same 85 participant IDs in the first column, samples in rows, complete continuous values with no NAs) and write the partial-correlation network as an edge list rather than a matrix?
Can BONOBO run with sparsify on at a 0.01 confidence level and delta fixed at 0.5 for my 18 log-transformed, centered endometriosis samples?

Our 96 brain RNA-seq samples (about 20,000 genes) were processed in four extraction batches and I want the batch effect removed. Depending on who you ask in the lab, that means a batch-corrected expression matrix to hand to other people, or batch-adjusted gene co-expression to build the regulatory network on, and I'm not sure which one I'm supposed to deliver. Batch is recorded per sample as numeric indicator columns.

Run SAMBAR on mutations_ucec.csv (248 endometrial tumours in rows, genes in columns, non-negative mutation counts) with exon_lengths.csv, cancer_genes.txt and c2.cp.kegg.gmt (MSigDB format), all sharing the same gene symbols, and cluster the tumours into between 2 and 6 subtypes.

For each of our 40 kidney cancer patients I need one number per transcription factor that captures that TF's regulatory strength in that patient, so we can relate it to survival. We have expression, a motif prior and a TF-TF PPI. I'm honestly not sure whether 'regulatory strength' here should mean how strongly the TF is wired to its targets or how active the TF is; my PI used both phrasings.

I've been reading about DRAGON, OTTER and GIRAFFE and they all sound powerful. Our lab has bulk transcriptomics, proteomics and some ATAC-seq peaks for a mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis, roughly 30 animals across three time points. Which of these should we apply, and what would we actually learn from each? We haven't settled on a specific hypothesis yet, and our PI wants something to show at the next lab meeting.

Can GIRAFFE estimate an activity score for every transcription factor in each of our 30 psoriasis skin samples? I have the gene-by-sample expression table, a TF-by-gene motif prior and a TF-TF PPI matrix with matching identifiers.

Can PUMA model the small RNAs from our mouse testis small-RNA-seq as regulators alongside the TFs? I have expression for 24 testes, a motif prior, a PPI and a small-RNA-to-target prior, but the annotation isn't finished: the small RNAs we picked could be miRNAs or piRNAs, and I genuinely don't know which yet.

Run BONOBO on expr_ms_lesions.tsv (27 multiple sclerosis lesion samples; log2-transformed and centered per gene; gene IDs in the first column, sample IDs in the header), but only write networks for samples MS_03, MS_11 and MS_19, saved as .csv files.
My PI told me to 'do the NetZoo thing, PANDA or LIONESS or something' on our zebrafish fin-regeneration RNA-seq before lab meeting. Which one should I run?

Run DRAGON on expr_cll_layer.csv and methyl_cll_layer.csv (same 110 patient IDs in rows, no missing cells). One thing I'm unsure about: the methylation file is either the continuous beta values or the binarized methylated/unmethylated calls (0/1) that another group derived, and both versions were saved under that name.

Run LIONESS-PANDA on expr_ra_synovium.tsv with motif_hs.txt and ppi_hs.txt to get a TF-to-gene network per column. I'm not sure which export this file is: the per-patient matrix (24 patients) or the version where a student averaged the patients into two columns, RA and control.

Run OTTER with seed_W_mm.tsv, ppi_tf_mm.tsv and coexp_liver.tsv; I have no expression file, only that co-expression file. I can't remember if coexp_liver.tsv is the full gene-by-gene correlation matrix for the cohort or the edge-by-sample table from our earlier LIONESS co-expression run.

We'd like a separate miRNA-protein partial-correlation network for each of our 50 heart-failure patients, from 300 serum miRNAs and a plasma proteomics panel measured on the same patients (complete, continuous, matching IDs). The catch: I don't remember whether the proteomics we got back is the 200-protein targeted panel or the 2,000-protein discovery panel, and the files are still on the CRO's server.
I want the list of genes differentially expressed between 12 drug-treated and 12 vehicle mouse hippocampi, with log2 fold changes and FDR-adjusted p-values like DESeq2 reports.

Using bulk expression and clinical follow-up for 400 lung adenocarcinoma patients, I need a model that predicts each new patient's overall-survival risk, something like a penalized Cox model that outputs a risk score, which I can then lock and apply to an external validation cohort of 150 patients from another hospital without refitting. Ideally the score would also show which genes drive the risk.

Is DRAGON able to link fecal metabolomics with colon-biopsy transcriptomics for our IBS study? Both tables are complete and continuous, but the metabolomics came from the 2023 recruitment wave and the biopsies may have been taken from a different group of volunteers; I'm still waiting to hear from the clinic whether they're the same 58 people.
I've put tumor_expr.tsv, motifs.txt, ppi.txt and clinical.tsv in the folder. Do whatever makes sense with them and give me figures for the paper.

I need a gene co-expression network for each of our 9 periodontitis gingival biopsies, with a p-value for every edge so I can filter them per sample. The matrix (genes in rows, sample IDs in the header) has been mean-centered per gene, but it came from a collaborator and I can't tell whether the values were log-transformed before centering.

Is OTTER able to run on CPU in single precision with 150 iterations and a step size (eta) of 1e-4, writing the result as an edge list? Inputs would be expression for 60 breast tumours (header row, gene IDs in the first column), a TF-by-gene seed edge list, and a TF-TF PPI edge list whose TFs are exactly the seed's TFs.

Can BONOBO build a co-expression network for each of my 6 rhesus macaque lymph node samples? The data are log2-transformed and centered per gene, with genes in rows and sample IDs in the header, and I'd like the per-sample matrices saved as HDF5 and computed in double precision.
Could you help me see how genes are connected in my sorghum heat-stress experiment?

Our grant renewal promises 'network-based insights' into Crohn's disease, and we have bulk RNA-seq from 150 ileal biopsies plus clinical data (disease activity, treatment, biopsy site). I need to propose a concrete analysis by Friday, but nobody has said what the network part should actually be or what question it should answer. We also have matched serology for most of the patients. What can we do?

Can PANDA build a single TF-to-gene regulatory network for our whole cohort of 48 mouse liver RNA-seq samples? I have the gene-by-sample expression matrix, a JASPAR-based motif prior and a mouse TF-TF PPI from STRING, all using the same gene symbols.

Can SAMBAR subtype our 160 pediatric medulloblastomas? The sequencing core sent a samples-by-genes variant-count matrix along with gene lengths, a cancer-gene list and a KEGG GMT, but their README doesn't say whether the counts are tumour-only somatic mutations or germline variant calls, and I can't tell from the file itself.

We ran a 48-gene NanoString inflammation panel on 600 rheumatoid arthritis patients recruited at four hospitals. I want to know how much of the co-expression between those 48 genes is associated with the hospital each sample came from, decomposed per covariate, with hospital coded as numeric indicator columns in a design table whose rows match the sample IDs exactly; each hospital contributed roughly 150 patients.

Run PANDA on expr_ipf.tsv with motif_hg38.tsv and ppi_hs.tsv, but use cobra_out/adjusted_coexpression.tsv (COBRA's adjusted gene-by-gene matrix, already checked to have the same gene IDs and order as the expression file) as the co-expression input instead of PANDA's own Pearson correlation.

Please run LIONESS-PUMA on expr_cll.tsv (36 CLL patients), motif_cll.txt, ppi_cll.txt, mir_targets.txt and mir_list.txt (one miRNA ID per line, every one present in the first column of mir_targets.txt) to get a TF/miRNA-to-gene network for every patient.
I uploaded counts_week0.tsv, counts_week4.tsv and counts_week12.tsv from our vaccine trial. Can you run the right workflow on them?
